title.value: New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
title.quote: # New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias

design.value: Two-stage genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of clinically diagnosed and 'proxy' Alzheimer's disease and related dementias
design.quote: We performed a two-stage genome-wide association study totaling 111,326 clinically diagnosed/‘proxy’ AD cases and 677,663 controls.

n.quote: We performed a two-stage genome-wide association study totaling 111,326 clinically diagnosed/‘proxy’ AD cases and 677,663 controls.

n_description.value: Clinically diagnosed and 'proxy' AD cases totalled across the two stages (111,326); the 677,663 controls are reported separately and are not included in this number
n_description.quote: We performed a two-stage genome-wide association study totaling 111,326 clinically diagnosed/‘proxy’ AD cases and 677,663 controls.

population.value: Individuals of European ancestry: clinically diagnosed AD cases, UK Biobank proxy-AD and related dementia (proxy-ADD) cases defined by parental dementia questionnaire data, and controls; stage I comprised 39,106 clinically diagnosed AD cases, 46,828 proxy-ADD cases and 401,577 controls, with stage II adding 25,392 AD cases and 276,086 controls
population.quote: All individuals included in stage I are of European ancestry; demographic data on these case–control studies are summarized in Supplementary Table

followup.value: For the genetic risk score analyses, predictive indices were computed at 5 years for population-based cohorts and 3 years for MCI cohorts
followup.quote: that is 5 years for population-based cohorts and 3 years for MCI cohorts

comparator.value: Controls without dementia; in the UK Biobank, individuals who did not report dementia or any family history of dementia
comparator.quote: In the UKBB, individuals who did not report dementia or any family history of dementia were used as controls; the analysis included 2,447 diagnosed cases, 46,828 proxy cases of dementia and 338,440 controls.

cohorts: AgeCoDe (German study on aging cognition and dementia)
AMC (additional, independent memory clinic cohort from Fundacio ACE)
HAN (BALTAZAR multicenter prospective memory clinic study)
UAN (memory clinic cohort from the Hospital Network Antwerp)
UHA (University of Halle memory clinic cohort)

outcomes.name: Number of independent risk loci associated with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADD) in the two-stage GWAS meta-analysis
outcomes.quote: We identified 75 independent loci for ADD; 33 had been reported previously, and 42 correspond to new signals at the time of this analysis.

outcomes.name: Number of loci new at the time of analysis
outcomes.quote: We found 75 risk loci, of which 42 were new at the time of analysis.

outcomes.name: Signals in previously known loci confirmed by the meta-analysis
outcomes.quote: this approach enabled us to define 39 signals in 33 loci already known to be associated with the risk of developing ADD

outcomes.name: Stage II follow-up of the new loci (replication in ADGC, CHARGE and FinnGen)
outcomes.effect_estimate: 17 of the 42 new loci reached P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in stage I; 25 reached it only after stage II follow-up
outcomes.quote: Of the 42 new loci, 17 had P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in stage I and 25 were associated with P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 after follow-up

outcomes.name: Genome-wide significance criterion for declaring a signal (including nominal stage II replication and concordant direction of effect)
outcomes.p_value: P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in the stage I and stage II meta-analysis, with P ≤ 0.05 in stage II
outcomes.quote: A signal was considered as significant on the genome-wide level if it (1) was nominally associated ( P ≤ 0.05) in stage II

outcomes.name: Loci with P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in the combined analysis but P > 0.05 in stage II (not counted as significant)
outcomes.quote: We also identified 6 loci with P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in the stage I and stage II analysis but with P > 0.05 in stage II

outcomes.name: Strongest rare-variant association at a known locus (TREM2 rs75932628)
Strongest association among the new loci (NCK2 rs143080277)
Pathway enrichment analysis of stage I association results (gene sets significant after correction for multiple testing)
outcomes.quote: Ninety-three gene sets were still statistically significant after correction for multiple testing ( q ≤ 0.05; and Supplementary Table ).

outcomes.name: Single-cell expression enrichment by brain cell type (Allen Brain Atlas)
outcomes.quote: Only the microglial expression reached a high level of significance ( P = 1.7 × 10 −8 ; Supplementary Table ); greater expression corresponded to a more significant association with ADD.

outcomes.name: Gene prioritization in the new loci
outcomes.effect_estimate: 31 tier 1 genes and 24 tier 2 genes prioritized across the 42 new loci
outcomes.quote: From all newly identified loci, this gene prioritization yielded 31 tier 1 genes and 24 tier 2.

outcomes.name: Association of the genetic risk score (GRS) with conversion to AD in population-based cohorts
outcomes.quote: the GRS was significantly associated with conversion to AD; this was shown in a fixed-effect meta-analysis (hazard ratio (HR) (95%CI) per average risk allele = 1.076 (1.064–1.088), P = 9.2 × 10 −40

outcomes.name: Association of the GRS with conversion to AD in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI)
outcomes.quote: Likewise, the GRS was significantly associated with AD conversion in patients with MCI (HR = 1.056 (1.040–1.072), P = 2.8 × 10 −12

outcomes.name: Increase in AD risk from the lowest to the highest GRS decile
outcomes.effect_estimate: 1.9-fold in population-based cohorts (HR = 1.93) and 1.6-fold in MCI cohorts (HR = 1.63)
outcomes.quote: the risk of conversion to AD rises with the number of risk alleles from non-APOE risk variants in the GRS by 1.9-fold in population-based cohorts (HR = 1.93 (1.75–2.13)

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The discovery analysis succeeded on its own terms: the two-stage meta-analysis identified 75 independent genome-wide significant loci for ADD, 33 previously reported and 42 new at the time of analysis.
primary_endpoint_status.quote: We identified 75 independent loci for ADD; 33 had been reported previously, and 42 correspond to new signals at the time of this analysis.

multiplicity.approach: Genome-wide significance threshold of P ≤ 5 × 10 −8 in the combined stage I and stage II meta-analysis, plus a requirement for nominal association (P ≤ 0.05) and concordant direction of effect in stage II; PLINK clumping and conditional analyses defined independent signals; q values were used for the pathway gene-set analyses
multiplicity.quote: A signal was considered as significant on the genome-wide level if it (1) was nominally associated ( P ≤ 0.05) in stage II

limitations: The UK Biobank proxy-AD designation is based on questionnaire data about parental dementia: 'This method has been used successfully in the past but is less specific than a clinical or pathological diagnosis of AD'.

Shared GRN and TMEM106B signals with frontotemporal dementia may partly reflect diagnostic misclassification: 'This association might be due to the misclassification of clinical diagnosis of AD and the presence of proxy-ADD cases in the UKBB.'

All individuals included in stage I are of European ancestry, and the document states that 'higher-powered GWASs of multiancestry populations will be particularly welcome' because 'GRSs developed with European-ancestry populations are known to be less effective with other ancestries'.
'identification of rare variants with very low frequencies is a major challenge for genetic studies, because available samples with sequencing data in AD are underpowered'
'gene–gene and gene–environment interactions have not yet been studied in detail'
'it is probable that additional, yet-unknown loci bear common variants modulating the risk for AD'
The added predictive value of the GRS was small: 'We found a small but consistent increase in the discrimination between AD converters and nonconverters'.
Gene prioritization was not performed in the complex IGH gene cluster locus (L27), and in five loci the prioritization score identified no molecular evidence beyond nearest-gene status.

risk_of_bias.judgement: A large share of stage I cases are UK Biobank proxy-ADD cases defined by parental dementia questionnaire, which the document itself says is less specific than clinical or pathological diagnosis.
risk_of_bias.quote: The UKBB’s proxy-AD designation is based on questionnaire data in which individuals are asked whether their parents had dementia.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Stage I is restricted to individuals of European ancestry, limiting transferability of the loci and of the GRS to other ancestries.
risk_of_bias.quote: All individuals included in stage I are of European ancestry

risk_of_bias.domain: Sample overlap between discovery and GRS validation
risk_of_bias.judgement: The Framingham Heart Study contributed to stage II of the GWAS from which the GRS weights were taken, and was excluded in a sensitivity analysis for that reason.
risk_of_bias.quote: excluded the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), as it was part of the stage II of the GWAS from which ORs for PRS computation were extracted

risk_of_bias.judgement: Nine of the reported loci had already been reported in three articles that used part of the same GWAS data, so they are not fully independent discoveries.
risk_of_bias.quote: were recently reported in three articles using part of the GWAS data included in our study

disagreements.question: Does including UK Biobank proxy-ADD cases distort the biology recovered by the GWAS?
disagreements.position: This document concludes that including proxy-ADD cases does not cause disease-relevant biological information to be missed and adds power.
disagreements.quote: This indicates that the inclusion of proxy-ADD cases does not cause disease-relevant biological information to be missed and underlines the additional power of this type of analysis.

disagreements.question: Have GWASs now characterized most of the common-variant component of AD risk?
disagreements.position: This document notes an existing estimate that fewer than 100 causal common variants may explain the entire AD risk, but argues that substantial further effort is still needed to characterize the missing genetic component.
disagreements.attributed_to: Bellenguez et al., this document, responding to 'a recent study'
disagreements.quote: A recent study estimated that fewer than 100 causal common variants may explain the entire AD risk ; if that estimate is correct, then our study might have already characterized a large proportion

disagreements.question: Are the reported signals driven by the UK Biobank proxy data?
disagreements.position: This document reports that none of the observed signals appeared to be especially driven by the UKBB data.
disagreements.quote: Similarly, none of the signals observed appeared to be especially driven by the UKBB data
